# Collect overdue invoices and resolve bad debt

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When an issued business invoice is overdue or its payment is disputed. Each overdue balance has a documented resolution, next collection action or approved accounting treatment.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Reconcile the receivable and evidence

agent-runnable


Match the signed terms, invoice, delivery evidence, credits and bank receipts. Confirm the correct debtor, due date and amount, and distinguish an actual dispute from a missing invoice or processing error.

- Sources: [GOV.UK late commercial payments](https://www.gov.uk/late-commercial-payments-interest-debt-recovery) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Choose a proportionate recovery approach

human · human approval required


The account owner reviews the customer relationship and finance exposure. Counsel confirms applicable collection rules and any proposed charges, demand, settlement or enforcement; do not apply one country's interest rules globally.

- Sources: [GOV.UK late commercial payments](https://www.gov.uk/late-commercial-payments-interest-debt-recovery) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Contact the debtor through the approved channel

human · human approval required


Send the authorized reminder or arrange a discussion using verified billing contacts. Ask for the dispute basis or payment commitment and record responses without threatening unapproved legal action.

- Sources: [GOV.UK late commercial payments](https://www.gov.uk/late-commercial-payments-interest-debt-recovery) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve escalation or a payment arrangement

human · human approval required


Review the documented response, recovery cost and the customer's ability to pay. Obtain authority for revised terms, service restrictions, collection-agent referral or proceedings and keep those actions within contract and local rules.

- Sources: [GOV.UK late commercial payments](https://www.gov.uk/late-commercial-payments-interest-debt-recovery) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Apply receipts or approved loss treatment

agent-runnable


Reconcile payments and approved credits to the ledger. Have the accountant determine any allowance or write-off, preserve recovery evidence and assign an owner and date for unresolved balances.

- Verify: Each overdue balance has a documented resolution, next collection action or approved accounting treatment.
- Sources: [GOV.UK late commercial payments](https://www.gov.uk/late-commercial-payments-interest-debt-recovery) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)
